newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Former Yugoslav president candidate for Serbia.
newsitem.headline: Former Yugoslav president candidate for Serbia.

text.p: The ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) on Friday decided on former Yugoslav president Zoran Lilic as its candidate to succeed Slobodan Milosevic as Serbian president in an election on September 21.

"Zoran Lilic has carried out a series of most responsible functions in Serbia and Yugoslavia and the Socialist Party of Serbia in a difficult period for our people and state," the SPS Main Board said in statement quoted by the Yugoslav news agency Tanjug.

"(Lilic) has vast experience in economy and international relations. In all the functions he has carried out so far he has shown a high level of responsibility towards the interests of our country and all its citizens," the SPS statement said.
The office of Serbian president has been vacant since Wednesday when Milosevic became president of Yugoslavia, which is made up of Serbia and Montenegro.
Diplomats said Lilic performed well in the mostly ceremonial post of federal president, has remained untarnished by scandal and would ensure Milosevic's uniterrupted control over Serbia.
Voting in the presidential contest and a simultaneous parliamentary election was set on Friday as September 21 by the acting Serbian president and speaker of parliament, Dragan Tomic.
